title: US Petrol Prices Stay Above $4 for a Record Number of Days
summaryZh: 美國油價今年已有158天高於每加侖4美元，創下紀錄。
summaryHi: अमेरिका में पेट्रोल इस साल रिकॉर्ड 158 दिन 4 डॉलर प्रति गैलन से ऊपर रहा।
summaryEs: La gasolina en EE. UU. lleva un récord de 158 días por encima de 4 dólares el galón.
summaryJa: 米国のガソリン価格、今年1ガロン4ドル超が158日に達し過去最多。
summaryKo: 미국 휘발유값이 올해 158일간 갤런당 4달러를 넘어 역대 최다를 기록했다.
summaryEn: US gas prices have been above $4 a gallon on a record 158 days this year.
paragraphs: Petrol prices in the United States have now stayed above $4 a gallon for a record number of days in a single year, adding to pressure on household budgets weeks before the midterm elections.

The national average for regular gasoline was $4.33 on Thursday, according to AAA, barely changed from a week earlier but more than a dollar higher than a year ago. Before the war with Iran began in February, drivers were paying under $3.

GasBuddy analyst Patrick De Haan said the average had been above $4 on 158 days in 2026, the most ever recorded in a calendar year. Diesel, which affects the cost of moving goods, has climbed to around $6.29 a gallon.

The surge stems from fighting around the Strait of Hormuz, which caused a historic shock to oil supplies. Crude is trading close to $100 a barrel, and although exports from the Gulf have recovered somewhat, higher shipping costs and ongoing risks are keeping prices up.

Fuel is also feeding wider inflation. Government figures released this week showed gas prices jumped more than 9 percent in September, accounting for over half of the month's overall price increase, while consumer sentiment has sunk close to a record low.
Petrol is very expensive in the United States this year. Americans call it gas.
On Thursday, the average price was $4.33 for one gallon. That is more than one dollar higher than last year. Before the war with Iran, the price was less than $3.
This year, the price has been over $4 on 158 days. That is a new record. No other year had so many days like this.
Why is gas so expensive? Oil comes on big ships from the Middle East. Because of the fighting there, less oil can come out. Oil now costs about $100 for one barrel.
Diesel is very expensive too. Many people are unhappy. They must pay more for food and other things. There is an important election in November, and prices are a big problem for voters.

Americans are paying more for gas than they have for years. On Thursday, the national average price for regular gasoline was $4.33 a gallon, according to the motoring group AAA. That is more than a dollar higher than a year ago.
An expert from GasBuddy said this week that prices have now been above $4 a gallon on 158 days in 2026. That is the highest number of days ever recorded in one calendar year.

The main reason is the war with Iran, which started in February. Fighting near the Strait of Hormuz, an important route for oil ships, has cut supplies. Crude oil is now around $100 a barrel, and diesel costs about $6.29 a gallon.

High fuel prices are also pushing up the cost of other things. New data showed that gas prices rose more than 9 percent from August to September, and that was more than half of the month's total price rise.
Many families are worried about money. Consumer confidence is close to its lowest level in more than 70 years, and the cost of living is a top issue before November's midterm elections.
Petrol prices in the United States have now stayed above $4 a gallon for a record number of days in a single year, adding to pressure on household budgets weeks before the midterm elections.

The national average for regular gasoline was $4.33 on Thursday, according to AAA, barely changed from a week earlier but more than a dollar higher than a year ago. Before the war with Iran began in February, drivers were paying under $3.

GasBuddy analyst Patrick De Haan said the average had been above $4 on 158 days in 2026, the most ever recorded in a calendar year. Diesel, which affects the cost of moving goods, has climbed to around $6.29 a gallon.

The surge stems from fighting around the Strait of Hormuz, which caused a historic shock to oil supplies. Crude is trading close to $100 a barrel, and although exports from the Gulf have recovered somewhat, higher shipping costs and ongoing risks are keeping prices up.

Fuel is also feeding wider inflation. Government figures released this week showed gas prices jumped more than 9 percent in September, accounting for over half of the month's overall price increase, while consumer sentiment has sunk close to a record low.

American motorists are enduring the longest stretch of $4-a-gallon petrol on record, as the economic fallout from the war with Iran continues to ripple through household finances ahead of next month's midterm elections.

According to AAA, the national average for regular unleaded stood at $4.33 on Thursday, more than a dollar above last year's level and well above the sub-$3 prices drivers enjoyed before hostilities broke out in February. GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan calculated that 2026 has now seen 158 days above the $4 mark, surpassing any previous calendar year.

The root cause is a severe supply shock triggered by fighting in the Strait of Hormuz. While Gulf exports have picked up in recent weeks, elevated shipping and insurance costs have kept crude hovering near $100 a barrel. Diesel, crucial for freight, is running at roughly $6.29.

The effects extend well beyond the forecourt. Inflation figures published this week revealed that petrol accounted for more than half of September's overall price rise, and consumer sentiment has slumped to near its lowest point in the 74-year history of the University of Michigan survey.
With affordability ranked as a leading concern among voters, fuel costs are likely to weigh heavily on the campaign's final weeks.

Fuel prices in the United States have remained above $4 a gallon for an unprecedented number of days in a single year, underscoring how profoundly the conflict with Iran has disrupted global energy markets and, consequently, the domestic economy.

Data from AAA indicate that the national average for regular gasoline reached $4.33 on Thursday, more than a dollar higher than twelve months earlier. GasBuddy analyst Patrick De Haan noted that the threshold of $4 has now been exceeded on 158 days in 2026, eclipsing every previous record.

Analysts attribute the persistent increase to a severe supply shock originating in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital corridor for oil shipments. Although exports from the Gulf have partially recovered, elevated transport costs and continuing volatility have kept crude prices close to $100 a barrel, while diesel, which is essential for freight, now exceeds $6 a gallon.

The repercussions are increasingly visible across the wider economy. Official figures show that gasoline was responsible for more than half of September's overall inflation, and consumer sentiment has deteriorated to near its lowest level in over seven decades.
Consequently, affordability has become a decisive issue for voters, and the trajectory of fuel prices may significantly influence the outcome of the forthcoming midterm elections.

noteJa.usage: of を伴うことが多い。upward / downward trajectory。
noteJa.exampleTr: その会社の売上は上昇傾向にある。

noteKo.usage: 흔히 of와 함께; upward / downward trajectory.
noteKo.exampleTr: 그 회사의 매출은 상승 추세에 있다.

noteEn.meaning: the direction in which something is developing over time.

transport.en: systems for moving people or goods
transport.ex: Public transport here is cheap and fast.

underscoring.en: showing clearly that something is important
underscoring.ex: The figures came out, underscoring the problem.

note.meaning: 強調、凸顯（重要性或事實）。
note.usage: 動詞 underscore，與 underline / highlight 同義；常以分詞構句出現於句尾：…, underscoring the need for…。

example.en: The floods hit again, underscoring the need for better drains.
example.zh: 洪水再度來襲，凸顯了改善排水系統的必要。

noteHi.meaning: किसी बात के महत्व को रेखांकित करना।
noteHi.usage: underline / highlight का पर्याय; वाक्य के अंत में कृदंत रूप में आम।
noteHi.exampleTr: बाढ़ फिर आई, जिससे बेहतर नालियों की ज़रूरत उजागर हुई।

noteEs.usage: Sinónimo de underline / highlight; frecuente al final de la frase: ..., underscoring the need for.
noteEs.exampleTr: Las inundaciones volvieron, subrayando la necesidad de mejores desagües.

noteJa.meaning: 強調する、浮き彫りにする。
noteJa.usage: underline / highlight と同義。文末の分詞構文で多い（…, underscoring the need for）。
noteJa.exampleTr: 洪水が再び起き、排水設備改善の必要性が浮き彫りになった。

noteKo.usage: underline / highlight와 동의; 문장 끝 분사구문으로 자주 쓰임.
noteKo.exampleTr: 홍수가 다시 발생해 배수 시설 개선의 필요성이 부각됐다.

noteEn.meaning: showing clearly that something is important or true.
noteEn.usage: Often a participle clause at the end: '..., underscoring the need for...'.

unhappy.ex: Customers are unhappy with the service.

university.ex: She wants to study law at university.

example.en: The company enjoyed unprecedented growth last year.
example.zh: 這家公司去年經歷了空前的成長。

note.meaning: 以前從未發生或見過的；空前的。
note.usage: 多為正式用語，常修飾 scale、level、growth、views 等名詞。

noteHi.exampleTr: पिछले साल कंपनी ने अभूतपूर्व वृद्धि देखी।
noteHi.meaning: जो पहले कभी न हुआ हो या न देखा गया हो।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक शब्द; scale, level, growth जैसे संज्ञाओं के साथ।

noteEs.exampleTr: La empresa tuvo un crecimiento sin precedentes el año pasado.
noteEs.meaning: que nunca ha ocurrido o se ha visto antes.
noteEs.usage: Formal; acompaña a sustantivos como scale, level, growth.

noteJa.exampleTr: その会社は昨年、前例のない成長を遂げた。
noteJa.meaning: これまでに起きたことも見たこともない。
noteJa.usage: フォーマルな語で、scale、level、growth などを修飾する。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 회사는 작년에 전례 없는 성장을 누렸다.
noteKo.usage: 격식 있는 말로 scale, level, growth 등을 수식한다.

noteEn.usage: A formal word, often used with 'scale', 'level' or 'growth'.

volatility.en: the quality of changing quickly and without warning

note.meaning: 波動性、不穩定性（價格、市場、情緒）。
note.usage: 不可數名詞，常與 market / price 連用；形容詞 volatile。

example.en: Price volatility makes it hard for farmers to plan.
example.zh: 價格波動使農民難以規劃。

noteHi.usage: अगणनीय; market / price के साथ। विशेषण volatile।
noteHi.exampleTr: कीमतों का उतार-चढ़ाव किसानों के लिए योजना बनाना कठिन करता है।

noteEs.usage: Sustantivo incontable con market / price. Adjetivo volatile.
noteEs.exampleTr: La volatilidad de los precios dificulta la planificación de los agricultores.

noteJa.usage: 不可算名詞。market / price と結びつく。形容詞 volatile。
noteJa.exampleTr: 価格の変動は農家の計画を難しくする。

noteKo.usage: 불가산 명사; market / price와 함께. 형용사 volatile.
noteKo.exampleTr: 가격 변동성 때문에 농민들은 계획을 세우기 어렵다.

noteEn.meaning: the quality of changing quickly and unpredictably.

voters.en: people who vote in an election

weeks.ex: We waited two weeks for the parcel.

weigh.en: weigh on: cause problems or worry for
weigh.ex: High rents weigh on small shops.

well.ex: She speaks Irish as well as English.

wider.ex: The benefits should reach the wider city.

worried.ex: She is worried about her exam.
